outcome: Not settled as of 10 October 2026. Since 26 January 2024 there are two new MLC-bearing preprints, each proving local connectivity of the Mandelbrot set on a restricted class of parameters: Kahn, Lyubich et al. (arXiv 2601.21905, Jan 2026, Elephant Eyes, MLC stated only in its last section and resting on cited work the authors describe as in preparation or to appear) and Kahn, Kapiamba and Lyubich (arXiv 2606.27272, 25 June 2026, MLC for parabolically bounded prime primitive families, which the authors say is not full MLC). Earlier partial results (Yoccoz c. 1990, Jiang 1995, Schleicher 1999, Kahn 2006-2007, Dudko-Lyubich 2018 and 2023) predate the window. No source found credits an AI system with any MLC result.
problem_asks: One question: is the Mandelbrot set M (the set of c in C for which the Julia set of z -> z^2 + c is connected) locally connected, i.e. locally connected at every point of M? Parts: (1) local connectedness of M at each point c of M; there is no separate part, parameter range, or number of cases. The statement does not name any consequence (density of hyperbolicity, local connectivity of Julia sets, a topological model of M, computability). Those follow from the conjecture but are not asked by the bullet as written. A positive answer (MLC holds) is what the conjecture asserts; the bullet asks the yes/no question.

events.what_happened: Jeremy Kahn, Alex Kapiamba and Mikhail Lyubich posted 'MLC for parabolically bounded primitive renormalization' (arXiv:2606.27272, math.DS, 73 pages, 5 figures, one version). Theorem A: every parabolically bounded family of prime primitive types has 'beau bounds' (a priori bounds). Theorem B: a family of prime primitive types with beau bounds and bounded puzzle Teichmuller diameter is rigid. Theorem C: every parabolically bounded family of prime primitive types is rigid, which the paper uses to deduce MLC at the parameters of those families. The introduction says: 'To fully resolve MLC, rigidity must be shown for all families of combinatorial types.' The paper also says it gives the first controlled a priori bounds for quadratic-like maps not satisfying the secondary limbs condition (SLC), per a search snippet of the introduction, not verified by me.
events.revisions: v1 only, as listed on the arXiv abstract page read 10 Oct 2026.
events.delivers: Rigidity, and so MLC (local connectivity of M), at every parameter whose renormalization type lies in a parabolically bounded family of prime primitive types. Here 'parabolically bounded' means a finite union of types plus parabolic tails, where a tail is a family {Phi_n o ... o Phi_q(M) : n >= q} built from limb insertions (q >= 2). 'Prime primitive' means small filled Julia sets are pairwise disjoint and the type is non-satellite. The types can approach parabolic parameters, i.e. the cusp of M. The paper states that combining the result with Dudko-Lyubich [DL23a] to cover families with finitely many primitive or satellite types and finitely many primitive parabolic tails 'is beyond the scope of this article'.
events.remains: Full MLC (rigidity for all families of combinatorial types); satellite types and families mixing finitely many primitive or satellite types with parabolic tails (stated as beyond scope); the general near-parabolic case, which the authors say these techniques should be a first step towards.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture: asserts MLC holds on a restricted class of parameters. No counterexample; does not claim full MLC.

events.what_happened: Jeremy Kahn and Mikhail Lyubich, 'A priori bounds for some infinitely renormalizable quadratics: IV. Elephant Eyes' (arXiv:2601.21905, one version, posted 29 Jan 2026). Abstract: 'we prove a priori bounds for an elephant eye combinatorics. Little M-copies specifying these combinatorics are allowed to converge to the cusp of the Mandelbrot set. To handle it, we develope a new geometric tool: uniform thin-thick decompositions for bordered Riemann surfaces.' The introduction says: 'we cover an unbounded situation, where the combinatorial types belongs to arbitrary 1/q-limbs'. Section 8 ('Local connectivity') says local connectivity of the relevant Julia sets follows from Hu and Jiang, and that 'MLC at the corresponding parameter values follows from the machinery developed in [L1]' together with little Mandelbrot copies on Ecalle-Voronin cylinders. A footnote 'added in Jan 2026' says a project with Alex Kapiamba was further developed and is 'to appear'. Preamble: 'The main result of this paper was obtained by the authors around 2010' and announced in talks from 2011; 'Here we reproduce the version of the article from Jan 2020.' The section text was read via a summarising fetch and is not quoted verbatim except where marked.
events.revisions: v1 only, as listed on the arXiv abstract page read 10 Oct 2026. The posted version reproduces a January 2020 draft; the authors date the main result to around 2010. I did not establish whether the 2020 draft was publicly circulated before the 29 Jan 2026 posting.
events.delivers: A priori bounds for an elephant-eye class of infinitely renormalizable combinatorics (an unbounded family across arbitrary 1/q-limbs, with bounding little copies allowed to degenerate to the cusp). In the paper's Section 8, MLC is stated at the corresponding parameter values, relying on the cited machinery of [L1] and on a project 'in preparation' / 'to appear'. The abstract itself claims a priori bounds, not MLC.
events.remains: Full MLC; every combinatorial class outside the elephant-eye family; the MLC corollary in Section 8 is stated only at the corresponding parameter values, and its argument relies on cited work I could not read.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture: a priori bounds, and per Section 8, MLC at the elephant-eye parameters. Partly conditional in the authors' own text on the cited unpublished or not-yet-appeared work.
people: Alex Kapiamba (named in a footnote as co-developing a related project; not an arXiv author)

events.what_happened: Dzmitry Dudko, 'On the MLC Conjecture and the Renormalization Theory in Complex Dynamics' (arXiv:2512.24171, one version, posted 30 Dec 2025; comment 'To appear in the Proceedings of the ICM 2026'). An expository note. It reports as established: MLC at the period-doubling Feigenbaum parameter (Theorem 4.1 of the cited work); a priori bounds and MLC for all ql-combinatorics of bounded type; and MLC along a real line and along any vein, attributed in the text to reference [14], which I could not identify. It states the program reduces to two open problems: completing the remaining unbounded satellite cases, and developing interpolation between positive and zero entropy settings. It lists Problem 4.3 (pseudo-Siegel a priori bounds in the remaining unbounded satellite ql cases) and Problem 4.4 (a virtual Molecule version of the near-degenerate regime) as open, and says solving them 'should imply the full MLC'.
events.delivers: No new theorem identified in the text I read; it is a status survey. It restates the cases above by attribution, each restricted as stated there (Feigenbaum parameter; bounded-type ql-combinatorics; real line and veins; satellite cases conditional on a strategy being 'fully realized').
events.direction: Reports MLC as open and gives a reduction; cuts towards MLC being true, not against.
people: Dzmitry Dudko (Stony Brook; co-author of several results it reports)

events.what_happened: Yueyang Wang, 'Local Connectivity of the Filled Julia Set Bundle over the Mandelbrot Set' (arXiv:2610.11793, sole author, posted 8 Oct 2026). Studies the non-escaping locus K_M = {(c,z) : c in M, z in K_c}, a model space for cubic capture straightening in the Inou-Kiwi framework. Abstract: 'We prove that boundary K_M has full Hausdorff dimension 4'; 'K_M is locally connected at every (c,z) with hyperbolic c in M'; 'local connectedness fails at some (c,z) with c real parabolic and z in K_c minus J_c'. The paper treats M only as a comparison point, noting that at certain real parabolic parameters both the parameter space and the filled Julia fibre are locally connected even though K_M is not.
events.delivers: Local connectivity of the two-variable bundle K_M at (c,z) with c hyperbolic; failure at some (c,z) with c real parabolic. It makes no claim about local connectivity of M itself at any parameter.
events.remains: The MLC question as stated is untouched.
events.direction: Not about MLC. It neither cuts for nor against the conjecture; it concerns a different object (K_M) that the paper contrasts with M.

Involvement is peripheral on the author's account; the 'discussions of mathematical arguments' clause is not specified further.

events.what_happened: Dzmitry Dudko, Yusheng Luo, Mikhail Lyubich, 'Uniform a priori bounds for neutral renormalization. Variation II: psi-ql Siegel maps' (arXiv:2509.23031; v1 27 Sep 2025, v2 1 Oct 2025). Extends uniform pseudo-Siegel bounds for neutral quadratic polynomials to psi-quadratic-like Siegel maps. Abstract does not mention the Mandelbrot set or MLC.
events.delivers: A priori bounds for Siegel maps in the psi-quadratic-like renormalization class: the degeneration of a Siegel disk is equidistributed among combinatorial intervals, except on transitional scales. No local connectivity result stated in the abstract.
events.remains: Local connectivity of M, which the abstract does not address.
events.direction: Not about MLC. A technical neighbour in the neutral-renormalization toolkit; the survey above cites neutral-family a priori bounds as part of its reports, without (as far as I read) naming this paper for an MLC conclusion.

events.what_happened: Alex Kapiamba, 'An optimal Yoccoz inequality for near-parabolic quadratic polynomials' (arXiv:2103.03211). First posted 4 Mar 2021; v2 15 Sep 2022; v3 3 Jan 2025; v4 13 Jan 2025 (in window). Abstract: describes degenerating external rays and parameter rays near parabolic points, and gives 'new bounds on the size of limbs of the Mandelbrot set', a quadratic Pommerenke-Levin-Yoccoz inequality in the near-parabolic setting. Abstract does not mention local connectivity.
events.revisions: v2 15 Sep 2022; v3 3 Jan 2025; v4 13 Jan 2025 (current; 'last revised 13 Jan 2025'). Revisions in the window do not move the date.
events.delivers: Bounds on the sizes of p/q-limbs (optimal for the 1/q-limbs) of M near parabolic parameters. A bound on limb sizes, not a statement about local connectivity.
events.time_since_posted: about 5.5 years since first posting; v4 about 9 months
events.direction: Not about MLC. Bounds limb sizes, a different quantity of M from its local connectivity.

events.what_happened: Alex Kapiamba, 'Non-degenerate near-parabolic renormalization' (arXiv:2210.06647). First posted 13 Oct 2022; v4 20 Feb 2026 ('Updated to include more explicit construction and analysis of petals'). Defines invariant classes for parabolic and near-parabolic renormalization, including the case where the multiplier is close to several roots of unity. Abstract does not mention MLC.
events.revisions: v4 20 Feb 2026 (in window; a revision, not a new date). Nothing in the window moves the first-posting date.
events.delivers: A general framework of near-parabolic renormalization operators; no local connectivity result stated in the abstract.
events.time_since_posted: about 4 years since first posting; v4 about 8 months
events.direction: Not about MLC; a tool-level paper in the near-parabolic renormalization area that the window results work in. I did not verify that the 2026 MLC papers use it.

events.what_happened: Dzmitry Dudko and Mikhail Lyubich, 'MLC at Feigenbaum points' (arXiv:2309.02107). v1 5 Sep 2023; v2 4 Dec 2023; v3 29 Dec 2025. Abstract: 'We prove a priori bounds for Feigenbaum quadratic polynomials, i.e., infinitely renormalizable polynomials f_c: z -> z^2+c of bounded type. It implies local connectivity of the corresponding Julia sets J(f_c) and MLC (local connectivity of the Mandelbrot set) at the corresponding parameters c.' It also says the MLC Conjecture 'was open for the most classical period-doubling Feigenbaum parameter as well as for the complex tripling renormalizations'. Journal: Publications Mathematiques de l'IHES, received 4 Dec 2023, accepted 25 Nov 2025, published online 2 June 2026, volume 143 (2026), per the journal's page. The first public written argument is the 5 Sep 2023 arXiv posting, so the journal dates do not move it.
events.revisions: v2 4 Dec 2023; v3 29 Dec 2025 (current). Journal publication online 2 June 2026 (PMIHES, vol. 143).
events.delivers: A priori bounds, and so MLC, at Feigenbaum parameters of quadratic polynomials (infinitely renormalizable of bounded type). Includes the period-doubling Feigenbaum parameter; the abstract also names the complex tripling renormalizations as open before this paper, without saying in the abstract which of them the bounds cover. Restricted to Feigenbaum (bounded-type) parameters.
events.remains: MLC at all other infinitely renormalizable parameters, including the unbounded satellite cases; full MLC.

events.what_happened: Dzmitry Dudko and Mikhail Lyubich, 'Local connectivity of the Mandelbrot set at some satellite parameters of bounded type' (arXiv:1808.10425). v1 30 Aug 2018; v2 30 Dec 2018; v3 29 Dec 2019; v4 13 Mar 2023. Abstract: M is locally connected at certain infinitely renormalizable parameters of bounded satellite type, the first examples of this kind, obtained via the unstable manifold of the pacman renormalization operator. Journal reference (Geometric and Functional Analysis, 2023) is from a search snippet, not checked on the arXiv page.
events.revisions: v2 30 Dec 2018; v3 29 Dec 2019; v4 13 Mar 2023. All before the window.
events.delivers: MLC at certain infinitely renormalizable parameters of bounded satellite type (near the main cardioid). Restricted to bounded satellite type and to 'certain' parameters in that class.
events.remains: Unbounded satellite cases (per the Dec 2025 Dudko survey), and all other infinitely renormalizable types; full MLC.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture: MLC holds at a restricted class of parameters.

events.what_happened: Dzmitry Dudko and Mikhail Lyubich, 'Uniform a priori bounds for neutral renormalization' (arXiv:2210.09280). v1 17 Oct 2022; v2 30 Dec 2024 ('adds references to further developments'). Abstract: uniform pseudo-Siegel a priori bounds for Siegel disks of bounded type; a Mother Hedgehog controlling the postcritical set for quadratic polynomials with a neutral periodic point; extension of Siegel/Pacman and near-parabolic renormalization theories to all near-neutral quadratic polynomials. Abstract does not mention MLC.
events.revisions: v2 30 Dec 2024 (in window; adds references; not a new date).
events.delivers: A priori bounds for Siegel disks of bounded type, uniform in scales, for quadratic polynomials with a neutral periodic point. No local connectivity result stated in the abstract.
events.direction: Not stated to be about MLC. The Dec 2025 survey uses neutral-family a priori bounds as part of its MLC reductions and cites a result it labels [16]; I did not establish that [16] is this paper.

events.what_happened: Dudko, Kahn and Lyubich, 'Local connectivity of the Mandelbrot set along the real line' (2022 manuscript). I could not find it on arXiv or elsewhere. Known only second-hand: a Dudko 2022 talk abstract says the key step is a priori bounds (compactness) for the quadratic-like renormalization operator, in the near-degenerate regime for maps with real combinatorics; a Lyubich 2023 Fields talk abstract says it 'confirms local connectivity of the Mandelbrot set M along the real line'; the Dec 2025 Dudko survey reports MLC along a real line as known. The survey bibliography entry came from a search snippet, because the fetched survey text was truncated before its bibliography.
events.revisions: Not posted to arXiv as far as found.
events.delivers: Local connectivity of M at real parameters (M intersected with the real line), per the second-hand descriptions; the abstract-level claim is restricted to real combinatorics. I have not verified how this relates to existing real-slice results.
events.doubts: Not verified. I have only talk abstracts and a survey's description, not the manuscript. The survey's sentence attributing real-line MLC to reference [14] is not resolved against this entry.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, restricted to real parameters.

events.what_happened: Jeremy Kahn, 'A priori bounds for some infinitely renormalizable quadratics: I. Bounded primitive combinatorics' (arXiv:math/0609045). v1 1 Sep 2006; v2 6 Sep 2006; v3 28 Dec 2023 (before the frozen revision). Abstract: a priori bounds for infinitely renormalizable quadratic polynomials with an infinite sequence of primitive renormalizations whose successive period ratios are bounded; 'This implies the local connectivity of the Mandelbrot set at the corresponding points.'
events.revisions: v2 6 Sep 2006; v3 28 Dec 2023 (before the frozen revision).
events.delivers: MLC at infinitely renormalizable parameters with bounded-ratio primitive combinatorics (bounded primitive type).
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, restricted to a combinatorial class.

events.what_happened: Jeremy Kahn and Mikhail Lyubich, 'A priori bounds for some infinitely renormalizable quadratics: II. Decorations' (arXiv:math/0609046). v1 1 Sep 2006; v2 12 Feb 2007. Abstract: for maps satisfying the decoration condition (a decoration is the part of M cut off by two external rays landing at a tip), a priori bounds are proved, 'They imply local connectivity of the corresponding Julia sets and the Mandelbrot set at the corresponding parameter values.'
events.delivers: MLC at the parameter values of infinitely renormalizable quadratics satisfying the decoration condition.
events.remains: Parameters outside the decoration condition; full MLC.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, restricted to decorations.

events.what_happened: Jeremy Kahn and Mikhail Lyubich, 'A priori bounds for some infinitely renormalizable quadratics: III. Molecules' (arXiv:0712.2444; Stony Brook IMS 2007/4). v1 14 Dec 2007, only version. Abstract: a priori bounds for infinitely renormalizable quadratic polynomials satisfying a molecule condition, which keeps the renormalization combinatorics away from satellite types; 'imply local connectivity of the corresponding Julia sets and the Mandelbrot set'.
events.delivers: MLC at parameters satisfying the molecule condition.
events.remains: Parameters outside the molecule condition; full MLC.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, restricted to the molecule condition.

events.what_happened: Dierk Schleicher, 'On Fibers and Local Connectivity of Mandelbrot and Multibrot Sets' (arXiv:math/9902155). v1 26 Feb 1999, only version. Abstract: new proofs that M is locally connected at every Misiurewicz point and at every point on the boundary of a hyperbolic component, via triviality of fibres; also shows local connectivity of M implies density of hyperbolicity. Published in Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics 72 (A Mandelbrot Jubilee, 2004), pp. 477-507, per the arXiv journal reference.
events.delivers: MLC at Misiurewicz points and at boundary points of hyperbolic components of M.
events.remains: All other points of M, including the infinitely renormalizable ones; full MLC.

events.what_happened: Yunping Jiang, 'Local connectivity of the Mandelbrot set at certain infinitely renormalizable points' (arXiv:math/9508212; MSRI 1995-063). v1 4 Aug 1995, only version. Abstract: constructs a subset of M that is dense on the boundary of M and consists only of infinitely renormalizable points, and proves M is locally connected at every point of that subset by finding bases of connected neighbourhoods directly.
events.delivers: MLC at a dense subset of boundary points of M, all infinitely renormalizable.
events.remains: The complement of that subset; full MLC.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, restricted to a dense subset of infinitely renormalizable boundary points.

events.what_happened: Jean-Christophe Yoccoz proved local connectivity of M at parameters that are not infinitely renormalizable (finitely renormalizable in the quadratic-like sense), around 1990. Reported in secondary sources only: the Wikipedia Mandelbrot set article ('established local connectivity of the Mandelbrot set at all finitely renormalizable parameters'); the Dec 2025 Dudko survey (Yoccoz's reduction of MLC to nested small copies); and the June 2026 Kahn-Kapiamba-Lyubich preprint's attributions. The original Yoccoz work (Orsay notes) was not opened. Date is the approximate year only.
events.delivers: MLC at parameters that are not infinitely renormalizable (the finitely renormalizable parameters), as the secondary sources state.
events.remains: All infinitely renormalizable parameters; full MLC.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, restricted to finitely renormalizable parameters.

summary: The problem is open on every source I could open that addresses its status. Wikipedia's Mandelbrot set article calls the full conjecture open and says local connectivity has been proved at many points; Dudko's Dec 2025 survey, which is the most recent overview I read in full, lists the remaining work as two open problems and says solving them 'should imply the full MLC'. Within the window (after 26 Jan 2024), the MLC-bearing results are: (1) Kahn and Lyubich, Elephant Eyes, posted 29 Jan 2026: a priori bounds for an elephant-eye class of combinatorics, with MLC at those parameters stated in Section 8 and resting on cited machinery and on a project the authors describe as in preparation or to appear (a close call: the abstract claims only a priori bounds, and a reader who discounts Section 8 gets a bounds result with no MLC on its face); (2) Kahn, Kapiamba and Lyubich, posted 25 June 2026: rigidity and so MLC for parabolically bounded families of prime primitive types, which the authors describe as a restricted class, with full MLC needing all families (the authors' own framing). The Feigenbaum result (Dudko-Lyubich) is pre-window by its first public arXiv posting (5 Sep 2023), and its PMIHES publication (online 2 June 2026) is in the window; under the first-public-argument rule it is dated 2023, but a judging pass that counts journal dates would place it in 2026. The Dudko-Kahn-Lyubich real-line result (2022) is known only second-hand: I could not obtain the manuscript, and I did not check it against existing real-slice literature. Non-MLC in-window items are recorded as discounted: Wang (8 Oct 2026, a different object, the bundle K_M), Dudko-Luo-Lyubich (Sept 2025, Siegel maps), and Kapiamba's two revisions (limb sizes, near-parabolic framework). AI involvement: no MLC event credits an AI system with mathematics. The only AI declaration I found in this area is in Wang's paper (ChatGPT and Codex, with the author's list of uses: language editing, LaTeX, notation checks, literature searches, numerical illustrations and 'discussions of mathematical arguments'; the author states responsibility for the proofs), which is a different object and so is discounted on scope, not on AI grounds. Other AI-related items checked and not MLC: OpenAI's openai/math repository (719 manuscripts in 372 families; I read the whole CONTENTS.md by title and found none on the Mandelbrot set, quadratic or Julia polynomials, renormalization, or complex dynamics; title screening only); Google DeepMind's Feb 2026 Gemini Deep Think blog (no MLC); a Claude-generated docs assessment in a personal GitHub repository (larsbx, PR #47, Oct 2026) that summarises an external survey and states that MLC is open; it is not a mathematical result and I do not record it as an event. The Quanta article of 26 Jan 2024 (the frozen date) describes the programme and includes the remark that 'Artificial intelligence is only beginning to be used to formulate substantive conjectures'; it is a press piece, not an event, and it names no AI system. Close calls: (a) whether a restricted-class theorem with the authors' own 'not full MLC' framing counts as progress on the problem as stated is the judging pass's call; (b) the Elephant Eyes Section 8 MLC corollary depends on material I could not read, and the 2020 draft it reproduces was not checked for prior public circulation, which would move its first-public-argument date; (c) the Feigenbaum date, as above.
competing_reading: For the June 2026 preprint: its restriction is substantive, since it excludes satellite types, mixed families, and the general near-parabolic case, so a reader could hold that it moves one class of parameters without moving the question. Against that: it proves rigidity, a structural claim about all parameters of its families, and the authors say it gives the first controlled a priori bounds for parameters not satisfying the secondary limbs condition, which is an advance on the method side. For the Elephant Eyes paper: the abstract claims only a priori bounds, and Section 8's MLC corollary is conditional on cited work, so one reading counts only the bounds (no MLC); the other counts the stated MLC corollary, which the authors present as following. For the Feigenbaum result: first public argument 2023 (predates the window) versus journal publication 2026 (inside it). For the real-line 2022 manuscript: a reader could count it as a full resolution on the real slice if the real-slice case is known to be settled elsewhere, which I did not check; such a reading would move it from a partial result to a non-result.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of arXiv 2606.27272: the definitions of 'beau bounds' and 'parabolically bounded' verbatim, the DKLP reference for the parabolic-tail diameter bound, and the reference list ([KL26] and [DKLP] were not located). (2) Any review, citing paper, or comment on 2606.27272 or 2601.21905 (none found, search index may lag; arXiv cited-by listings were not checked). (3) The unposted projects cited in Elephant Eyes Section 8 ([L1] and the Kapiamba project), and whether any has since been posted. (4) Whether the January 2020 draft reproduced in Elephant Eyes was publicly available before 29 Jan 2026. (5) The 2022 Dudko-Kahn-Lyubich real-line manuscript, and a check of the real-slice literature to see whether the real-line case is new. (6) The journal's referee record for Dudko-Lyubich PMIHES is not needed for the date rule, but would bear on the 'checked by' field.
